x.bio: High fidelity research. Dm for promo

tweets.text:
"DAPD: Dual-Anchored Policy Distillation"

This paper fixes a subtle failure in self-distillation for reasoning models.

In OPSD, the teacher gets to peek at the reference answer during training, but the student has to reason without it at inference. So the student can learn to act like it knows something it cannot actually know.

DAPD adds anchors so teacher and student are compared under matched information, then balances clean reference guidance with on-policy rollout guidance.

In their experiment, Qwen3-4B got +2 over OPSD on average, and this holds up to 32B.

Read more:
https://t.co/pjppzibw31

"Reusing Rollouts under Policy Lag"

LLM RL wastes a lot of compute generating rollouts. So people reuse the same rollouts for multiple updates, but the model keeps changing, which makes old rollouts increasingly off-policy.

This paper suggests a better way to think about that mismatch, where you don’t just ask how likely the current token is now, you also ask how likely the prefix was that got the model to this token in the first place.

The exact prefix correction is too unstable because it multiplies ratios across many tokens. PNPO uses the prefix geometric mean instead, keeping the causal prefix signal while avoiding exploding weights.

This makes rollout reuse safer when policy lag gets larger.

In the 4-epoch setting, PNPO beats GSPO by 3 points Avg@32 and reaches similar performance with 150 rollout batches instead of 600.

Read more:
https://t.co/z44VFQReDO

Been thinking about why AI diffusion has been slow. 

It’s because we are asking users to understand our nerdy lab speak.

We greet them with a blank window and ask them to write a prompt. Then they have to pick a model, decide whether they need an agent, and somehow know what context windows, reasoning, MCP, memory, and skills are.

Most people don’t care. They need a thing done. If you can give them something that does that, they’re happy.

I think we will see that breakthrough product in the next 12 months.

x.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

tweets.text:
Correct take. 99% of tokens in the world will get consumed in an enterprise context. 

They will be for writing code, combing through insane amounts of life sciences research, automating manufacturing, securing enterprises, detecting fraud, and thousands of other tasks like this that have significant economic value. This is both where the cost of AI can be most justified but also where the impact of parallel workers doing tasks on your behalf is most useful.

Even the agents that most impact consumers will often be wrapped up as just end to end services where the consumer doesn’t think about there being an AI system on the other end, like faster insurance or onboarding to a bank.

The key though is it’s going to take years for diffusion of agents across the economy because workflows have to re-engineered to incorporate AI, which is a complete change to how most work happens today. Anyone who’s expecting this to happen overnight should be updating their timelines.

Google is in talks to acquire Mechanize, a startup that creates high quality RL coding environments, for $1.5B. This is the biggest AI data business acquisition since Scale!

Mechanize was founded ~1yr ago, and has a team 35-50 who are each paid ~$400k/yr to create ~1 good task/week for a cost of ~$8k/task. In their own words, “almost anything that you struggle to get coding agents to do could be a good task, if implemented correctly”.

They were last valued at $500M 3mos ago. Jeff Dean, Google’s Chief Scientist was on the cap table (but it was reported just 15mins ago that he’s leaving Google after 27yrs to his own AI for science startup)!

Mechanize were known to be one of the premium sources of coding training data for models and I suspect Google in-housing this is a way to prevent others from getting a hold of this data, in addition to the process talent on the team who come from Epoch AI, the guys who made the FrontierMath benchmark amongst other things. It’s also validation for the dozens of companies in this space that M&A is still very much on the cards if your data is critical enough.

Tremendous outcome if it goes through!
